A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NFT research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the revised title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original 7B and 32B math-reasoning experiments, algorithm comparisons, training curves, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including Table 1 and the ablation figures.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and new Appendix B extend the stated reward input from binary labels to values in [0,1], allowing rewards to weight both terms of the existing loss. The implicit negative policy, binary training algorithm, clipping, and prompt weighting remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DAPO-Math-17k and evaluate on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC 2023, MATH500, OlympiadBench, and Minerva Math. The continuous-reward extension has no corresponding dataset or evaluated task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DPO, GRPO, Dr. GRPO, DAPO, and RFT for 7B comparisons, and DAPO and RFT for 32B comparisons. Figure 5 also retains the same released-model comparators. DPO's InfoNCA implementation is documented in both versions.

E3.justification: The settings in v1 Appendix B match v3 Appendix C, including model configurations, rollout budgets, answers per prompt, context lengths, validation sampling, verifiers, and prompt processing. Table 1 retains avg@32 for AIME/AMC and avg@1 for the other benchmarks.

E4.justification: The negative-feedback and entropy analyses, three-way prompt-weighting ablation, and clipping-parameter sensitivity study are retained with identical evidence in Figures 8–10. The new continuous-reward appendix is theoretical, not an added empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 6 reports the same 3–4 independent experiments per algorithm and mean ± standard deviation. Uncertainty displays are retained, with no added run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 is identical: NFT's average scores remain 51.7 for 7B and 59.2 for 32B, compared with DAPO's 51.2 and 59.9. Figures 5–11 retain the same benchmark scores, training curves, and ablation results; no new empirical outcomes appear in the appendices.

T1.justification: New Appendix B formalizes continuous rewards as optimality probabilities and adds Theorem B.1 with a derivative-based argument for the reward-weighted target distribution, assuming accurate mean rewards and unlimited data and capacity. This extends the existing objective's analysis; the original negative-policy theorem and on-policy equivalence proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its performance-gap claim from SL versus RL to RFT versus RL. The central claims about learning from negative feedback, competitive math performance, and strict-on-policy equivalence with GRPO remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds the hypothesis that larger models already memorize sufficiently well, making reflection on mistakes a bottleneck. v3 also explicitly discusses applicability to continuous rewards while removing Section 6's claim of easy adaptation to masked language models.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit repository URL for the existing math-verify verifier. The project link, hardware, hyperparameters, implementation choices, and validation instructions otherwise remain; moving experimental details to Appendix C does not establish changed settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds Levine's probabilistic-inference reference and Yan et al.'s off-policy-guidance work, while removing the masked-language-model discussion and several background references. The main positioning relative to supervised learning, RL, DPO, and implicit modeling is retained.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and author information, edits wording and policy notation, corrects erroneous Eq. B references to Eq. 9, adds an LLM-use disclosure, and moves setup prose into the appendix. The main section sequence and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR styling and running headers, reflows text and equations, and places Figures 9 and 10 side by side above their discussion. All eleven figures and Table 1 are retained without substantive graphical or table-structure changes.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the continuous-reward extension through explicit assumptions and a derivation, narrows the SL-versus-RL performance claim to RFT, and fixes confusing equation references. These modestly improve precision and usability. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the continuous-reward extension remains untested, limiting the overall gain.
